params.requirement: Decides in the nightly memory round which relation names mean the same thing and which candidate pairs are the same person, place or thing. It needs the most careful judgement available, since a wrong merge corrupts memory, and strictly structured output. It runs once a night and never while anybody waits, so speed and price matter little.

model.description: MODEL_JUDGE - the identity judgement of the nightly canonicalisation round (ruling Q1). This is the one place in the hive that deliberately carries the STRONGEST model available, not the cheapest that works: the verdict is written into the store as an alias and every later read consumes it. The default is a top-tier placeholder rather than an empty string, because an unconfigured judge would silently skip the canonicalisation round every night; set it explicitly at rollout.

api_key.description: Provider API key. Deprecated, removed in 0.63.0: name a grant in credential_grant_id instead (#801).

credential_grant_id.description: GH #801: the grant this cell presents to get its provider credential SEALED from an access hive instead of carrying a key. It ships EMPTY, which is no grant at all; whoever grows the cell (the builder recipe or the colony's own template) sets it through `override_params`, and the credential then arrives over the credential v-lane and is opened in RAM only. Immutable: a new grant is a new instance.

provider_extra.description: The provider overlay of this cell, shipped empty. Its deliberation budget lived here as provider_extra.reasoning.effort (GH #138, a literal of this cell's own `params` in place of the colony-wide `MEMORY_REASONING_JUDGE`) until GH #1300 moved it to the flat `reasoning_effort` setting: an overlay `reasoning` key is sent verbatim, which the Anthropic Messages wire refuses, while the flat param takes each wire's own form. A key set here still wins over the flat param.

external_timeout_ms_row.description: GH #1097: not read by the cell -- the catalogue row its `external_timeout_ms` and `cell.message_timeout` are derived from (the timeout chain, docs/cell-types.md § llm): the row of the model this cell is born on. A manifest that bears it on another row derives both again from that row.

reasoning_effort.description: GH #1300: how long the model deliberates before it answers, in the provider's shorthand (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `none` = off, or the lowest effort a model that cannot switch thinking off takes; passed through, not checked against a list). It ships `medium`, the effort every shipped llm cell runs at unless its instance says otherwise: an instance sets it through `override_params` on this cell's path, and a registry push that names no effort resets it to this birth value. On the chat-completions wire it goes out as `"reasoning": {"effort": ...}` (default `reasoning_wire`), on the Anthropic Messages wire as `output_config.effort`; `none` switches thinking off in the form the model takes. A `reasoning` object, where one is set, outranks it; a model whose catalogue `supported_params` omits the field never receives it.

description.purpose: Judges IDENTITY for the nightly canonicalisation round (0.2.0 P5, rulings Q1/Q3/Q5): which predicate keys name the same relation, and which entity candidate pairs are the same person, place or thing. It is the persisting twin of the extractor - the extractor keeps a new turn on the axes that exist, this one repairs the axes that already fell apart. Top tier on purpose, once a night, never per turn.
description.use_when: Called by dream-glue once per consolidation run, after the dreamer's verdicts are parked and before the supersession arithmetic, with the predicate inventory and the fuzzy entity candidates in one payload.
description.not_in_scope: No store access and no effect of its own: dream-glue turns the verdict into set_alias / reject_pair / canonicalize, all additive and revertible. It never deletes, never rewrites a written value, and never judges supersession (that is arithmetic). It also never invents a name - every value it returns has to come from the payload.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one assistant turn holding the judgement JSON {predicates:[{alias,canonical}], entities:[{alias,canonical}], different:[{dimension,left,right}]}. hop.finish_reason='error' makes dream-glue skip the round and continue with the rest of the run instead of leaving it hanging.
description.consumes_meaning: system.instructions.text: the judgement contract, handed over by dream-glue (an llm cell has no params.system - the prompt travels in the message). messages[]: the predicate inventory with the subjects each key is used on, plus the candidate entity pairs with the facts of both sides. The one body without messages[] is a params-only push on the hive's `in_model` door (GH #858): an empty system slot and a params slot the cell merges into its live params, answered with nothing.
examples: predicates 'Lieblingseditor' and 'favorite_editor', both used on subject 'user' -> {"predicates":[{"alias":"Lieblingseditor","canonical":"favorite_editor"}]}
entity pair ('ashford','ashfrd'), one with two facts and one with a single typo-shaped fact -> {"entities":[{"alias":"elvse","canonical":"elvese"}]}
entity pair ('robin','robyn'), each with its own birthday fact -> {"different":[{"dimension":"subject","left":"robin","right":"robyn"}]} - remembered, so the pair is never proposed again
